subject.title: Add loop-aware compaction guard for saturated sessions

question: Should saturated-session compaction recovery be designed as a new agents.defaults.compaction.guard policy, or should it extend the existing tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard and compaction safeguard surfaces?
rationale: The requested behavior adds public config/defaults, reset-recommendation policy, and session-state semantics while current main already has a narrower overlapping post-compaction guard under a different namespace.

options.title: Extend Existing Guard Surfaces
options.body: Use the existing tool-loop and compaction safeguard paths as the base, adding tail-risk classification and validation without publishing a second overlapping namespace first.

options.title: Adopt New Compaction Namespace
options.body: Accept a new agents.defaults.compaction.guard contract after defining coexistence, migration, defaults, docs, and reset-recommendation semantics.

options.title: Defer To Broader Trackers
options.body: Keep this issue as design context while prioritizing the broader compaction-continuity and rate-limit issues separately.

recommendation.title: Extend Existing Guard Surfaces
recommendation.body: Use the existing tool-loop and compaction safeguard paths as the base, adding tail-risk classification and validation without publishing a second overlapping namespace first.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across compaction safeguard, runner refactors, config policy, and post-compaction guard follow-up work.
